batch: 4 (chs 20-24, the rebellious history, the breach, the two sisters, the wife's death)

units.characteristics: God acting for his name's sake; the self-loathing that the memory of forgiven sin produces
units.gist: GEM - the rebellious history (Egypt, wilderness, generations); the refrain 'I ACTED FOR THE SAKE OF MY NAME, that it should not be profaned' (forbearance grounded in God's own name, not the people's worth); the sober 'I gave them statutes that were not good' (given over to consequences); and the fruit of grace - 'THERE YOU SHALL REMEMBER your ways... and YOU SHALL LOATHE YOURSELVES for all the evils'; 'I deal with you for MY NAME'S SAKE, NOT according to your evil ways'

units.characteristics: the groaning prophet; the dross in the furnace; the missing intercessor
units.gist: GEM - the sword song - the prophet 'GROAN with breaking heart and bitter grief before their eyes' (his grief a sign); the bloody city's catalogue; 'the house of Israel has become DROSS to me... in the furnace'; and the searching lament - 'I SOUGHT FOR A MAN among them who should build up the wall and STAND IN THE BREACH before me for the land, that I should not destroy it, BUT I FOUND NONE' - the tragic absence of an intercessor

units.characteristics: escalating lust; self-disgust that does not stop the sin; the cup
units.gist: Oholah (Samaria) and Oholibah (Jerusalem), the two whoring sisters, lusting after Assyria, Babylon, Egypt; the escalation - Oholibah 'more corrupt than her sister'; 'after she was defiled she TURNED FROM THEM IN DISGUST, yet she INCREASED her whoring' (self-disgust that does not stop the craving); 'you shall drink your sister's CUP, deep and large... a cup of horror' - the addictive recoil, and its measured cup

units.characteristics: the deepest personal loss conscripted as a sign; grief held in - sigh, but not aloud
units.gist: GEM - the boiling pot (the bloody city); then the hardest sign - 'I am about to take THE DELIGHT OF YOUR EYES away from you at a stroke; yet you shall NOT MOURN or weep... SIGH, BUT NOT ALOUD; make no mourning for the dead'; Ezekiel's WIFE dies that evening, and he obeys - his suppressed, silent grief made a sign of a people who will be too stunned to mourn when the temple (the delight of their eyes) falls
